content: HomePolice Station RatesNew Regulations Effective 22 December 2025Police Station Legal Aid Rates 2025/26The Criminal Legal Aid (General and Remuneration) (Amendment) Regulations 2025 have introduced the most significant overhaul of police station fees in over a decade. Updated: December 7, 2025• Fact CheckedNew Harmonised Fee£320.00Universal fixed fee for all 245 schemes (excluding VAT).Previous Rates£223.52 (National) / £Varied (London)Escape Threshold£650.00New unified threshold. Claims exceeding this amount revert to hourly rates.Effective DateDec 22Applies to all cases with a UFN assigned on or after this date.Understanding the 2025 AmendmentsOn 22 December 2025, the Ministry of Justice implemented the Criminal Legal Aid (General and Remuneration) (Amendment) Regulations 2025 (SI 2025/1251). This legislation fundamentally changes how police station advice and assistance is remunerated in England and Wales.Previously, the legal aid system relied on a complex matrix of 245 separate "schemes", each with its own fixed fee ranging from £223.52 (National) to £315.86 (Heathrow). This disparity often meant that representatives doing identical work in different counties were paid vastly different amounts.The Key Change: HarmonisationThe 2025 Regulations abolish these regional variations for the fixed fee. There is now a single, harmonised Fixed Fee of £320.00 applicable to every police station scheme in England and Wales.Impact Analysis: Winners and Losers The "Winners"Providers in "National" rate areas see the biggest uplift. For schemes like Birmingham, Manchester, Leeds, and most non-London counties, the fee jumps significantly.Old National Rate£223.52New Rate£320.00+£96.48 per case (+43%) London & HeathrowFor London schemes, the increase is more modest.Heathrow was previously the highest paid scheme and sees a very slight increase or effective freeze relative to inflation.Heathrow (Old):£315.86Brent (Old):£241.18New Uniform Rate:£320.00The New Escape Fee MechanismThe Escape Fee is a safety valve for complex cases. If the work you do on a case—calculated at hourly rates—exceeds a certain threshold, you are paid for the actual time spent rather than the fixed fee.Crucial Update: Alongside the fixed fee harmonisation, the Escape Fee Threshold has also been harmonised to £650.00.How to Calculate an Escape Fee (Post-Dec 2025)1. Calculate Your Profit CostsSum up attendance, travel and waiting time using the applicable hourly rates from Schedule 4. Rates vary by category (own solicitor, duty solicitor, unsocial hours, serious offence).Own Solicitor RatesAttendance (London):£58.97/hrAttendance (National):£54.57/hrTravel/Waiting:£30.22/hrDuty Solicitor RatesAttendance (London):£58.97/hrAttendance (National):£54.57/hrTravel/Wait (London):£58.97/hrTravel/Wait (National):£54.57/hr2. Compare to Threshold✓Total > £650.00?You claim the full hourly amount (e.g., £750).✗Total ≤ £650.00?You claim the Fixed Fee (£320.00).Enhanced Rates Also AvailableUnsocial Hours: £72.46/hr (attendance + travel/waiting)Serious Offence (London): £68.21/hr attendanceSerious Offence (National): £62.96/hr attendanceSerious + Unsocial: £83.95/hr attendanceUse Our Escape Fee CalculatorKey PointsYou cannot mix the fixed fee and hourly rates. You claim the fixed fee unless your hourly profit costs exceed £650.Travel and waiting time are factored into the hourly rate calculation. They are included within the £320 fixed fee and are not paid on top unless the case escapes.Mileage (45p per mile for first 10,000 miles, 25p thereafter) is a separate disbursement — it is not part of the profit costs calculation.Claiming Multiple FeesA common query is whether multiple fees can be claimed for attending the same client. The rules remain unchanged by the 2025 regulations. The key test is whether the matters are "truly separate". Claim Two Fees If:Different Occasions: Offences committed on clearly different dates.Unconnected Matters: Arrested for Assault today, but also questioned about a historic Burglary from 3 months ago.Separate Investigations: Matters that would likely not be joined on the same indictment. Single Fee Only If:Same Incident: Multiple charges arising from one event (e.g., Drink Drive + Assault PC).Linked Series: 5 shopliftings from the same Tesco over a week.Multiple Interviews: Interviewed at 10am and again at 4pm for the same matter (claims as one attendance).Transitional Arrangements (UFN Dates)The rate you can claim is strictly determined by the Unique File Number (UFN) date assigned to the case.Before 22 Dec 2025Must claim Old Rates (e.g., £223.52 National).On/After 22 Dec 2025Claims New Rate (£320.00).Training Guides & ResourcesTraining guides, Rep Wiki, and
